title: API does not make much sense
body:
Hello, 
I am trying to experiment with the serial API and find it rather disappointing experience.
Problems encountered:
1.  cannot read list of available ports in the system. In my app, I need to show the list of ports to the user and let them pick the correct one to use. Using the built-in dialog (which looks horrible, by the way) is not the way I need to do it in my app.
2. when testing in HTML page from file://... URL, getPorts() always returns empty list. I do not understand the rationale behind this, when local page wants to access local resource and it is just impossible... makes no sense.
3. similar problem with `reader.read()` - the device is sending data back, but those are never read and the respective routine remains in an infinite loop. 
4. Information provided about ports (SerialPort.getInfo()) does not return enough information to keep any kind of persistent information for subsequent use of the same ports. For instance, there is Arduino device (as telegraphy keyer) and a CAT interface, both using the same chip as USB/serial interface. Both have signature 0x0403:0x6001 and there is no way to find any distinguishing feature: neither the system comm port number (COM3 or COM4), nor serial number (in my case A900VLOI and A5XK3RJT, respectively). Coming back to my point 1, I could only read the list of devices *after* they are accessed. Well, if I have to invoke the horrible dialog window and click the potentially needed ports first (one by one!), why not do this at once in the beginning and save time and click-effort? However, without the key identifiers, how can I make any decisions?

I am not willing to take part in the development, but I believe if you look at the issues, you will know what to do.
Thank you for consideration.
Jindra
